# automox_server_group (Resource)

An Automox server group. Devices inherit their scan interval and OS-update behaviour from the group they belong to, and policies target groups rather than individual devices.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Server groups are how Automox targets devices: policies attach to groups
# rather than to individual endpoints.

data "automox_server_groups" "default" {
  # The organization's default group has an empty name; the console shows it as
  # "Default". Every other group is parented to it.
  name = ""
}

resource "automox_server_group" "workstations" {
  name                   = "Corporate Workstations"
  parent_server_group_id = data.automox_server_groups.default.server_groups[0].id
  refresh_interval       = 1440
  ui_color               = "#059F1D"
  notes                  = "Managed by Terraform"

  # enable_os_auto_update and enable_wsus are three-state. Leaving one unset
  # means each device keeps its current behaviour, which is NOT the same as
  # setting it to false and actively changing every device in the group.
  enable_os_auto_update = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Server group name.
- `parent_server_group_id` (Number) ID of the parent group. Use the organization's default group to create a top-level group; the default group is the one whose parent is itself.
- `refresh_interval` (Number) How often devices in this group scan for updates, in minutes. Automox requires between 240 (4 hours) and 1440 (24 hours).

### Optional

- `enable_os_auto_update` (Boolean) Whether devices in this group use the operating system's own automatic updates.

Leaving this unset is **not** the same as `false`: unset means each device keeps whatever it is already configured to do, while `false` actively disables OS auto-update on every device in the group.
- `enable_wsus` (Boolean) Whether Windows devices in this group patch from a WSUS server rather than from Windows Update.

As with `enable_os_auto_update`, unset and `false` differ: unset leaves each device's existing behaviour alone, `false` forces Windows Update.
- `notes` (String) Free-text notes.
- `policies` (List of Number) IDs of policies attached to this group.

This relationship has two sides: setting `server_groups` on an `automox_policy` also adds that policy here. The attribute is therefore computed as well as optional, so a group whose configuration does not mention policies accepts whatever Automox reports rather than trying to detach policies attached from the other side.
- `ui_color` (String) Colour used for this group in the Automox console, as `#RRGGBB`.
- `wsus_server` (String) WSUS server URL, for example `https://wsus.example.com:8530`. Used with `enable_wsus`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) Server group ID.
- `organization_id` (Number) Organization this group belongs to.
- `server_count` (Number) Number of devices currently in this group. Changes as devices enroll and move, independently of this configuration.
- `uuid` (String) Server group UUID. Required by `automox_scheduled_window`, which identifies groups by UUID rather than by ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Server groups import by their integer ID.
terraform import automox_server_group.workstations 230685
```
